notes:
Meet the companion. The mascot is now called the companion, and its settings have a place of their own: Settings → Companion. It never needed the AI assistant to keep you company, so it no longer sits under AI.

Ogam, the first companion, comes as a small download from Settings → Companion. He breathes, blinks and changes expression with what you are doing, stays quiet while you write, and speaks at natural pauses: a reached target, a long pause, coming back to a project. Every comment can tell you why it appeared, and «Less of this» or «Don't mention this again» make him quieter. He never makes himself louder.

While you revise, the companion can point you to what your enabled checks found and take you to each place. For spelling, grammar, synonyms and double spaces it shows the fix before and after, and applies it only when you choose it, as one step you can undo. It never changes your text on its own.

Ogam's face moves. His brows rise and fall, he blinks, closes his eyes when he is content or sleepy, smiles, and opens his mouth when he speaks: twelve expressions instead of three pictures. He shows his face larger, and his idle movement stops when nothing is happening, so he costs almost no processor time.

Settings → Companion offers an Update when a new version of the companions is out. Your companion keeps working on the version you have until you choose it.

When you have asked the companion for less of a kind of comment, «Why?» now says so. Settings → Companion can open the folder where it keeps what it learned, and if one of its pictures cannot be loaded it says so once and carries on with the simpler drawing.

macOS: Corylus is not notarized yet, so Gatekeeper may say the app cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified. Right-click (or Control-click) Corylus.app, choose Open, then Open again. Only needed once per downloaded copy.
